item.title: Re: A Deconstruction of the Foundations Modus Operandi (SCP)
item.content:encoded:
Well, you obviously know your SCP. Better than I do, anyway. If there are any inconsistencies with the Foundationverse, I'm definitely not expert enough to identify them.

+ show block
– hide block

I still have something to say about the bacteria, though. I like the backstory and the fancy microbiology I barely grasp, however:

…later stages of the anomalous strain cause those who are infected to lose higher cognitive brain function, who are then compelled to spread the disease.

That's textbook zombies. The nuances you've added to the bacteria's mechanism don't really change it in that regard - the outcome is still bad meat with no brains.

…the infected aren't undead or anything; they'll die just as easy as any other human.

The T-Virus zombies from RE are also technically alive and are also just deprived of high brain functions. Not less textbook zombie for it.


That's the only part I'm having trouble digesting. But aside from that, looks good to me. Then again, me also knows jack shit about top clearance levels, XK-Scenarios and all that jazz, so you gotta get that critted from someone else.

Good luck!

item.title: Re: A Deconstruction of the Foundations Modus Operandi (SCP)
item.content:encoded:
Well, I guess you could call it a zombie plague, but I suppose it's more nuanced than that. I mean, the infected aren't undead or anything; they'll die just as easy as any other human. Moreover, it'll be written in such a way to make it interesting. For instance, it is implied the phenomenon manifested due to the lynching of the poor Jewish gentlemen, who was repeatedly burned as a form of torture. The reason why the infection can only be destroyed through incineration is because those that killed Parisian Man used fire to burn him, even though he wasn't infected. This triggered some kind of anomalous event, fuelled by the victims hate. The murderers would've succumb to the very plague they accused him of causing, with the only escape being death through fire (coincidently, the same way they killed him.)

Moreover, not to bash 008 (it was a product of its time), but mine will go into more detail about the anomalous disease. For instance, the researchers find the bacteria lacks efflux pumps, drug-inactivating enzymes, or any other mechanism known to confer resistance to antibiotics. Despite this, antibiotics have no effect whatsoever. The minutiae may not be for everyone, but I like writing with a heavily scientific tone, sort of like an academic research paper.

+ show block
– hide block

Frankly, I don't think it's even necessary for you to write an SCP if this story is
all you'll be focusing on - you could just write it in as a tale around 1609. But
then again, that's completely up to you.

The SCP will be interesting in and of itself (ideally, anyway). The 1609 realisation is just kind of an oh shit ending I want to wrap it. Moreover, by writing a tale, it'd be difficult to explore the characterisation of Miller. The repeated neutralisation denials are what drive him to ask "Why are the Foundation so adamant on containing anomalies we can't learn anything from, even when they're dangerous? Is it because we're afraid of unintended consequences, or do the O5s have their own agenda?"

How exactly does Miller find out about the conspiracy? Everything in the
Foundation is under lock, key and blast gate when it comes to any sort of
administration - let alone the O5.

So, Miller actually has Level 4 Access (justified, in my opinion, because he's working with an anomaly that could theoretically cause an XK-Class End-of-the-World Scenario.) That being said, he obviously doesn't have access to the O5 councils dirty little secrets. The way in which he finds out is as follows:

Miller is actually a GOC mole, trying to change the Foundation from the inside. By conferring with contacts within the GOC, he finds out that the supposed 1609 event never happened, and there's no record of the people that supposedly died ever existing. In fact, the GOC had never even heard of 1609. From that, Miller pieces the rest together. This would leave the reader wondering who to believe. Are the GOC lying to Miller, or are the Foundation lying and using fictional botched neutralisation attempts as a form of propaganda?

(This is subject to change, but the most believable way in which I could justify Miller working it out. Nobody wants a terrible cliche in which he just magically hacks the database)

Why kill Miller ala FBI/FSB if they can just amnesticize him or change his memories?
It's simple, quiet and cheap. More so than staging a breach is, at any rate.

They kill him because he's a mole. Obviously, they can't just make a Level 4 project lead disappear because people would ask questions. They can't be honest either, because they don't want people to know the Foundation was infiltrated. Therefore they orchestrate a controlled containment breach, and order Beta-7 to kill everyone within the quarantine zone (which, conveniently, includes Miller).

How are you planning to convey the whole story? I'm assuming you're going to
write a different format after the article - no way is O5 letting a story like that be
featured in one.

Everything up to the breach log can be accessed normally. The breach log ends with Miller typing something on his terminal when Beta-7 breach his office and shoot him. The final file will be behind level 5 access. So you go through the rigamarole of Level 5 Classified Warnings etcetera etcetera, there's mention of a memetic kill agent, then the file opens with "Welcome, Overseer." Therefore, it's sort of implied the reader is a member of the O5 Council in this scenario. The contents of the final file are what Miller was writing on his terminal, detailing the shady stuff the O5's are doing, how 1609 doesn't actually exist etc. It's implied he was going to try to send this information to the GOC before he was killed.

So yeah, that will be the end. Hopefully it'll leave the reader wondering who was telling the truth, the Foundation or the GOC. I want to leave the reader questioning the Foundations obsession with containing everything, rather than outright destroying anomalies that pose a threat to humanity.

item.title: A Deconstruction of the Foundations Modus Operandi (SCP)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, history, Foundation politics

Page Layout (Optional): Classic SCP layout; addenda will include a neutralisation proposal, interview with site-director, and a containment breach. This addenda will be presented in a novel style in the form an official document/folder (for an idea, see SCP-5859.)

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation hears reports of people becoming infected with a seemingly untreatable strain of the Bubonic Plague. MTF Beta-7 ("Maz Hatters") are deployed to control the situation. What follows is a deconstruction of the Foundations M.O: Secure, Contain, Protect.

► Additional details
▼ Additional details

Central Narrative: The SCP in question is a the corpse of a 14th century Parisian male discovered deep within the catacombs of Paris (stumbled upon by Patient-Zero, an overeager urban explorer). Due to the anti-Semitic slur scorched into the corpse's chest, Foundation historians have theorised that the corpse was murdered due to the Christian persecution of the Jewish populace admist the onset of the Bubonic Plague.

The corpse is the cause of the outbreak. Exposure results in infection from an anomalous strain of Yersinia pestis. Initial stages of infection operate much the same way as a non-anomalous strain. However, rather than dying, the later stages of the anomalous strain cause those who are infected to lose higher cognitive brain function, who are then compelled to spread the disease.

Once the SCP is secured, the plot follows the project lead, Dr. Stephen Miller, in a vain attempt to neutralise the corpse due to the inherent risk of an XK-Class scenario if a containment breach were to occur. Unfortunately, his proposal is denied. He's given the usual spiel about how its a safe class object, how he'd be more at home at the Global Occult Coalition, about how historically attempted neutralisation of objects has often made things worse, which is why the Foundation contains rather than Destroy, Destroy, Destroy. The Site Director cites SCP-1609 as an example; it was a teleporting chair that the GOC put through a wood chipper. Now, it's a murderous pile of splinters.

What follows is a breach. An area of Site-19 becomes infected, and Beta-7 are deployed to clean up the mess, resulting in the death of Miller.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: We discover that SCP-1609 (and many others) are completely fabricated. They don't exist. They are nothing but Foundation propaganda, a way to convince Foundation personnel that the GOC are incompetent and the Foundations way is the correct way… the only way, to deal with the anomalous. Moreover, they serve as a warning to those who would try to preemptively neutralise an anomalous object. The breach was orchestrated by the O5s to kill Miller after discovering the secret.

Additional Notes: Rough draft available on request.
